reference: python-control 0.10.2 (margin, nyquist_response, feedback, step_response, frequency_response), numpy/scipy polynomial algebra and root finding, an independently coded Nyquist winding-number integrator, a high-resolution delay-differential-equation solution of the closed-loop FOPDT step response, and the published tuning rules of Ziegler & Nichols (1942), Rivera/Morari/Skogestad (1986) and Astrom & Hagglund (2004) implemented from their printed formulae.

tolerance: Rational LTI algebra the tool claims to implement exactly: 1e-10 relative on normalised polynomial coefficients, 1e-9 on pole locations, 1e-11 on |L(jw)|, 1e-9 deg on arg L(jw) (modulo 360 deg), 1e-7 relative on gain/phase/delay margins and crossover frequencies, 1e-8 of the response span on step responses, 1e-12 relative on tuning-rule outputs (closed-form arithmetic), exact integer equality on Nyquist counts. The closed-loop step response of a dead-time loop is NOT rational; there the criterion is that the tool declares its Pade approximation, that the error falls with Pade order, and that the default order 3 stays within 2 % of the exact delay-differential-equation solution.

Tool: fixed-step RK4 at h = 1/(20 mu) = 5e-05 s, 20000000 steps, decimation 5001. Reference: scipy solve_ivp(Radau, rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-13) at the tool's own recorded instants. [tool: RK4 (fixed step), h = 0.00005 s, 20000000 steps, 3559 ms; worst at t = 999.9499500000001 s]

Default coil loop with every non-linear element disabled (instantaneous actuator, no deadband, hysteresis, noise or quantisation, continuous controller, no sensor lag). The largest difference between the non-linear run and the linear closed-loop prediction, as a fraction of the setpoint step, is measured against the step size (plant curvature) and against the integration step (integrator error). Deviation at h/16: 10 K -> 82.8213 %, 3 K -> 10.8215 %, 1 K -> 2.6859 %, 0.3 K -> 0.6865 %, 0.1 K -> 0.2082 %, 0.03 K -> 0.0522 %. At dw = 0.01 K, against h: h=1.0000 -> 0.4165 %, h=0.5000 -> 0.2046 %, h=0.2500 -> 0.0997 %, h=0.1250 -> 0.0490 %, h=0.0625 -> 0.0266 %. Measured order in h = 1.030.

The page ships a 19-case reference run behind its Validate tab. This entry audits what those cases are, not whether they pass. 49 of 63 checked quantities are this page's own arithmetic or the output of a previous run of the same code; only 14 are read from the cited publication, and none of the 19 is compared against an independent implementation. The pass criterion is therefore that the tab SAYS so, per FRAMEWORK_V2_SPEC §3 ("a self-check that re-evaluates the tool's own formula does not count towards benchmarked, and the UI must not present it as validation").
The gain and phase margin printed on the Frequency tab for the default coil loop must equal LIN.margins on the loop the app assembled (display rounding 0.05).

provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_regelkring.py from the sources this artifact cites. That generator was re-run on 2026-10-16 with the control package installed (0.10.2), in a reference directory from which regelkring_ref.json had first been removed, and wrote a file byte-identical to the deployed corpus (126 060 B); so no case reuses a stored reference that this tree cannot re-derive.
